name: Zachary Sunberg
title: Assistant Professor (current university directory and CV; a2026 paper biography says Associate Professor)
department: Ann and H. J. Smead Aerospace Engineering Sciences; Computer Science by courtesy
fitReason: Strong AI/control foundation with a newly verified physical humanoid project. A useful fit for uncertainty-aware autonomy and integration of learned and model-based control, rather than only simulated POMDP benchmarks.

physicalEvidence.summary: August21,2026 GOLEM deploys ALMI adversarial-RL standing on a real Unitree H1-2 and demonstrates push recovery. Learned YOLO-World perception supports visual-servoed picking of already-loosened battery screws. Walking tests use the vendor controller; ALMI walking was unreliable. Language-memory tests are simulated. ADCL's current roster lists first author Max Conway, tying this collaborative hardware work to Sunberg's group.

shortVisit.summary: Current lab lists prior visiting scholars and a Vanderbilt doctoral visitor for summer2025, but no current external-master's visitor or summer2027 invitation was verified. Historical summer presence earns no opportunity points.

name: Nikolaus Correll
title: Viola D. Hank Professor; Director, Physical AI and Robotics Initiative
fitReason: Direct embodied-AI, learned perception/control and real manipulation focus. The newly established Notre Dame group offers relevant research directions, while the lab move makes local hardware and short-visit readiness important unknowns.

physicalEvidence.summary: Corresponding coauthor of the August2026 GOLEM Unitree H1-2 humanoid study. Its real battery manipulation and learned balancing are substantial physical evidence; the work spans the Boulder-to-Notre-Dame transition, and the reviewed sources do not establish that the tested robot is now at Notre Dame. The current lab distinguishes Notre Dame students from continuing Boulder students.
